The complaint was filed by the anti-corruption group Wag Kang Ku-corrupt, which sought an investigation into Dela Rosa's absence and potential violations of Senate rules.

MANILA, Philippines – Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa has asked the Senate ethics committee to dismiss a complaint against him over his prolonged absence from the Senate.

In a response submitted to the Senate committee on ethics and privileges, Dela Rosa, through his legal counsel Israelito Torreon, sought the dismissal of a complaint filed by anti-corruption group Wag Kang Ku-corrupt in February.
The group had asked the Senate panel to investigate the senator’s prolonged absence, determine whether he violated Senate rules and ethical standards, and impose appropriate sanctions if warranted.

In a notice, the Senate ethics panel informed dela Rosa that they had found the complaint to be compliant with requirements “both in form and in substance” following an executive session on October 22. The panel directed Dela Rosa to submit a written response within 15 days of receiving the notice.
Dela Rosa’s office confirmed receiving the notice on November 19.
In his response, Torreon argued that the complaint should be dismissed for “insufficiency in form and substance, and for failure to state any offense cognizable by the Committee.”

Dela Rosa also asked the committee to hold the proceedings in abeyance pending the resolution of his camp’s motion for reconsideration of the Supreme Court ruling that denied his plea for a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the enforcement of the International Criminal Court warrant.
He also asked the committee to deny the motion included in the complaint, seeking the suspension of his Senate office’s operations, including the release of salaries and operational expenses.

“In the event the Committee proceeds further, furnish respondent with copies of all records on which it intends to rely, and afford him a hearing, through counsel, with the opportunity to examine the complainants and their witnesses and to present evidence,” he added.
Senate ethics committee chairperson Vicente “Tito” Sotto III confirmed receiving Dela Rosa’s response.

“I received the answer via email on Saturday, November 21, 2026, 8:51 pm. It was submitted through his counsel and not signed by him personally. This answer will be considered in the next Ethics hearing that will be scheduled at the soonest time,” Sotto told reporters in a Viber message.
In October, Dela Rosa again asked the SC to reverse its earlier ruling denying his plea for a TRO against the enforcement of the ICC arrest warrant.
Dela Rosa is among the former officials of the Rodrigo Duterte administration implicated in the bloody anti-drug campaign, which human rights organizations say resulted in nearly 30,000 deaths.

The ICC Pre-Trial Chamber I issued an arrest warrant against the senator in November 2025 over his alleged role in the drug war. The court identified him as a co-perpetrator in the case, saying those involved “controlled a structure of power” that enabled them to “direct and control the actions” of those who carried out the killings.
The warrant remained under seal until May 11 of this year, when it was made public.

Dela Rosa had been absent from the Senate for months before appearing on May 11 to support Senator Alan Peter Cayetano’s bid for the Senate presidency. He then remained inside the Senate building for three days as he sought refuge from possible arrest.

A shooting incident erupted on the night of May 13, allegedly triggered by Senate Sergeant-at-Arms Mao Aplasca, Dela Rosa’s Philippine Military Academy classmate. Hours later, at around 2:30 am, Dela Rosa left the Senate building, accompanied by his political ally, Senator Robin Padilla.
Dela Rosa has since stayed out of public view.
In seeking a reconsideration of the SC ruling, Dela Rosa’s lawyer argued that the enforcement posture against the senator had “escalated” while the motion remained unresolved.

The motion also cited developments since the original petition, including the Department of the Interior and Local Government’s declaration of Dela Rosa as “armed and dangerous” and the P50-million bounty offered for his arrest. – Rappler.com
